A.a: T1- Map 1 shows superimposed boundaries. E2- European countries like Britain and France drew the borders without caring about the African groups that lived there. A3- This means many groups got split up.
The boundaries are geometric. They are straight lines that follow latitude and longitude, like the border between Egypt and Sudan.
Most of the borders are superimposed boundaries because they were drawn by Europeans at the Berlin Conference, not by Africans.
A lot of the borders on Map 1 are just straight lines, especially in the Sahara where Algeria, Libya, and Egypt meet. Colonizers drew them with a ruler.
Map 1 shows the borders of the colonies that European countries owned in Africa.
They are antecedent boundaries because they were there before people lived there.
The type of boundary is a colonial boundary because Africa was colonized.

B.a: T1- The colonial boundaries are straight lines but the cultural boundaries are curvy. E2- Map 1 has straight borders but on Map 2 groups like the Hausa have uneven edges. A3- This shows Europeans didn't follow where groups lived.
The European boundaries split culture groups apart. For example the Ewe on Map 2 are split between the Gold Coast and Togo on Map 1.
The colonial borders ignore where ethnic groups live, while the cultural boundaries on Map 2 follow where each group actually lives.
Colonial boundaries put a lot of different groups into one colony. Nigeria on Map 1 has the Hausa, Yoruba, and Igbo from Map 2 all together.
Map 1 shows colonies and Map 2 shows culture groups.
The European boundaries are straight lines.
Map 2 has more groups than Map 1.
Map 1 is the whole continent of Africa and Map 2 is only West Africa.

C.a: T1- One outcome is civil war. E2- In Nigeria the borders put the Igbo, Yoruba, and Hausa in one country, and the Igbo tried to break away as Biafra. A3- This happened because different groups were forced to share one government.
Colonial borders split ethnic groups between different countries, so some groups want to reunite, which causes border disputes, like the Somali people in Ethiopia and Kenya.
Because the borders combined the Muslim north and the Christian south of Sudan into the same country, there was a long civil war until South Sudan became independent in 2011.
Many African countries have weak national unity because the colonial lines grouped many different ethnic groups together, so people are more loyal to their tribe than to the country.
Colonial boundaries caused a lot of problems in Africa.
Africans today speak English and French because of colonization.
There are lots of wars in Africa.
The boundaries divided Africa into colonies for European countries.

D.a: T1- Europeans believed their culture was superior to African cultures. E2- At the Berlin Conference they split up Africa without inviting any Africans. A3- This shows they didn't think Africans deserved a say.
Europeans thought Africans were uncivilized, so missionaries came to convert them to Christianity and get rid of their traditional religions.
The Europeans saw African cultures as primitive and made Africans learn European languages like French in colonial schools.
Europeans looked down on African kingdoms and ignored them when they drew the borders, because they thought their own way of governing was the only right way.
Ethnocentrism is when you think your culture is better than other cultures.
Europeans thought they were better than Africans.
European colonization reflected ethnocentrism because they colonized Africa for its resources.
The Europeans took over Africa and drew new borders.

E.a: T1- Many colonies were drawn to include the coast. E2- The Belgian Congo has a small strip that reaches the Atlantic Ocean. A3- This let them ship rubber out of the Congo to Europe.
The colonies on the coast like the Gold Coast and Togo stretch inland from the ocean so Europeans could get raw materials from the interior to ports.
Almost every European colony has a coastline so they could export resources like gold and diamonds on ships back to Europe.
Gambia is drawn around the Gambia River, which the British used to move peanuts and other goods out to the sea for export.
Europeans wanted Africa's resources, like gold and rubber.
The boundaries are straight lines drawn by Europeans.
Britain had the most colonies, so they got the most resources.
The Belgian Congo is very big and in the middle of Africa.

F.a: T1- Colonization affected languages to a great degree. E2- Many countries still use the colonizer's language as their official language, like French in Senegal and English in Nigeria. A3- These languages are used in government and schools, but people still speak African languages at home too.
To a large degree but not completely. Portuguese is the official language of Angola and Mozambique, but most people there also speak native languages.
Colonization affected languages to a moderate degree. English and French are used in government and business, but hundreds of indigenous languages like Swahili and Hausa are still spoken every day.
It had a big impact because English is an official language in Ghana and Nigeria and is taught in schools.
Colonization affected African languages because Europeans brought their languages to Africa.
Colonization affected languages to a great degree.
People in Africa speak many different languages.
Colonization changed the languages in Africa a lot.

G.a: T1- Map 2 shows culture groups, not religions. E2- People in the same culture group can practice different religions, like Yoruba who are Muslim or Christian. A3- So you can't use the map to know where religions are.
The map only shows West Africa, so it doesn't tell you anything about religion in North or East Africa.
Map 2 shows ethnic groups, but religions like Islam and Christianity spread across many ethnic groups through trade and missionaries, so the groups don't match religions.
Map 2 doesn't have a date, so it can't show how religions changed over time as people converted to Christianity or Islam.
Map 2 is hard to read because all the patterns look the same.
The map shows where religions are because each culture group has its own religion.
Map 2 only shows culture groups like the Hausa and Yoruba.
